title: RunManifest
description: meta/manifest.json — what each stage of a run consumed, produced and ran under. It exists because the first draft of the plan asserted that the existing --resume and Prefect caching 'stay valid' for independently re-runnable stages, and that is not true as written: session_metadata.txt records no completed-phase list (pipeline.py:590), Prefect caching is keyed around whole-phase tasks, and legacy checkpoint read errors already fall back to empty state (pipeline.py:502). Re-running one stage would leave every downstream artifact falsely current. The manifest makes staleness derivable instead of assumed: a stage is current only if every input it recorded still hashes to what it recorded. Legacy and staged runs keep SEPARATE manifests so the two modes cannot collide on filenames.

mode.description: 'staged' = driven by `python -m dr2_podcast.stage`. 'legacy' = the monolithic runner, which keeps working throughout this plan (--legacy-smart-author) and writes its own manifest file.

artifact.description: Path relative to the run directory, e.g. 'research/research_framing.md'.

outcome.description: 'transport' is a malformed or empty response that was retried. It is recorded separately from a revision round on purpose: conflating them silently shortens a loop bounded at 3 rounds.

status.description: 'stale' is set on a downstream stage when an input it recorded no longer hashes to what it recorded — never silently reused.

identity.description: Model and configuration the stage ran under. A change here is an input change: the same inputs under a different model are not the same run.
